text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- This is a teroristic act which will most probably be politicised but the victims are ordinary people, Franciscan guardian Stjepan Duvnjak says after grenade attack on monastery in Kraljeva Sutjeska.

- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation police investigating attack on monastery say the grenades were fired from the nearby hill of Tesevo and a policeman who was guarding the building was slightly injured by debris.

- Moslem chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, receives April 6th award which commemorates liberation of Sarajevo from Nazis in 1945. He said the city had acquired international respect during the 1992-95 war and had to do everything to hold on to that respect.

- Bosnia's opposition Social Democratic Party (SDP) completes two-day convention by electing Zlatko Lagumdzija to the post of new party president. The party adopts declaration calling for opposition to ethnic division of Bosnia.

- Deputies in the parliament who also perform duties in Bosnia's administration have to quit one of these positions to conform to constitution, Bosnia's ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action executive board says.
- The international arbiter for the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko, William Farrand, will -- after some delays -- open his office in the town on Wednesday, diplomatic sources say.

- Although the working atmosphere in Bosnia's council of ministers is good, the results it has achieved so far after almost 100 days are less than satisfactory, Bosnian Foreign Minister Jadranko Prlic says.

- An international donors conference for Bosnia's reconstruction is expected to take place in May and joint institutions will probably adopt all necessary laws by that time, Prlic says. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
